implementation.source_manifest_reuse_boundary: The source manifest was prepared for the Futaleufu asset review. Pacuare reuses only the same CC0 Fern 02 files and recorded rights provenance as generic humid-rainforest-floor morphology; it makes no Pacuare species, ecology, geography, or field-survey claim.
implementation.shadow_policy: scanned and procedural short ground cover self-shadow suppressed; shrubs and moss-rock analogs retain scene shading
implementation.material_packaging_contract: Fern and active small-fir materials persist explicit Nanite and InstancedStaticMeshes usage flags; final Pacuare PIE MapCheck is zero errors and zero warnings.

matched_capture_comparison.baseline: The retained humid-atmosphere V1 guide, river-eye, and solver-rapid frames are the closest pre-change fixed-camera baseline.
matched_capture_comparison.reason: The complete deterministic map regeneration also refreshes temporal water and renderer state, so small whole-frame water deltas cannot be attributed to the fern substitution.
matched_capture_comparison.finding: The four scanned forms add localized fine frond silhouettes and break up part of the former single procedural groundcover family without creating a new dominant color band or entering the water corridor. At the canonical camera distance the change is modest; adult canopy, broad bank shape, and water defects remain visually dominant.

accepted_findings: The regenerated L_UpperHuacas map remains reference-runnable and contains four tagged, non-colliding scanned-fern HISM actors with 3,640 instances.
Seventy percent of the accepted 5,200 near-bank groundcover targets now use four scanned fern forms; 1,560 procedural placements remain for density and morphological variation.
Every placement retains the established source-Landscape height, dry-bank, slope, full-centerline, complete-visible-water-width, and protected-solver-strip gates.
The CC0 source materials now persist explicit Nanite and hierarchical-instancing usage flags, removing the two packaging warnings found by the first runnable-map pass.
The project-owned canopy, shrub population, moss-rock layer, total foliage budget, cooked field, collision, water geometry, hydraulics, bathymetry, and raft forces remain unchanged.
The final editor build, five native Pacuare tests, focused runnable-map PIE gate, and MapCheck all pass.
remaining_photoreal_defects: Adult canopy crowns, trunks, branches, and shrub lobes remain angular, repetitive, and visibly procedural at guide-seat and river-eye distances.
The reused fern assets are generic morphology analogs; no qualified Pacuare ecology review has accepted their species, density, age, season, disturbance, or wetness pattern.
Near-bank ground still lacks continuous leaf litter, roots, vines, epiphytes, deadwood, wet sediment, small plants, and sub-meter microtopography.
The broad smooth banks and 30 m source context do not resolve surveyed bank breaklines, boulders, bedrock structure, waterfalls, or rapid-scale gorge geometry.
The foreground water remains dark, broad, and visually smooth, with weak breaking-wave volume, aeration, foam complexity, spray, mist, rock-contact plumes, refraction, and riverbed transition.
Atmospheric depth, rainy-season lighting, cloud response, wind, moving canopy, and wet-surface variation remain incomplete.
The canonical environment-only frames do not validate raft, crew, paddle, water-occlusion, guide-line, hazard, or rescue readability in this updated bank context.
No measured desktop or VR performance profile has accepted the added scanned population on named target hardware.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A qualified Pacuare rafting guide accepts Upper Huacas route identity, water levels, entry and exit, named hazards, guide lines, rescue routes, and gameplay sightlines in runnable guide-eye views.

A geospatial reviewer accepts coordinate transforms, vertical datum, route stationing, shoreline and bank breaklines, higher-resolution terrain, rocks, waterfalls, and the declared boundary between sourced terrain and procedural gap fill.

A hydraulic reviewer accepts calibrated and converged flow bands against observed Upper Huacas discharge, surface elevations, velocities, Froude behavior, rapid-specific features, and hazard response.

A regional ecologist and environment-art reviewer accepts species and morphology analog use, density, age classes, season, wetness, disturbance, geology, ground cover, lighting, and rainforest atmosphere.

A water-VFX and character/equipment art review accepts water transmission, raft and crew occlusion, waves, holes, rollers, aeration, spray, foam, bank intersections, paddles, animation, and close-range asset quality.

Measured full-run desktop and VR profiles pass release frame-time, memory, streaming, shader, collision, capsize, recovery, stability, comfort, and complete-run gameplay budgets on named target hardware.
